summary: Conditional constraint and unchanged-model control. Inspected all four premise dossiers and exact existing definitions. In the explicitly selected profile supportsEsse := m.Causes, actual reflexivity, necessity of a and b, OtherDirectedPotentialCause for each, and WellFoundedUnionNecessarySupport imply ¬(a ≠ b), without an excluded-middle premise. Apply each potential clause at the selected base world, using the other necessary bearer's presence there. Its possible causal edge is witnessed at a root-accessible world; necessity supplies source presence there, giving both opposite UnionNecessarySupport edges. Pinned Mathlib.Order.RelClasses.WellFounded.asymmetric rules out the pair. This is negative non-distinctness, not an unqualified constructive identity theorem; no intensity, weak degree bound, invariance, no-contingent-ground or explanatory-token assumption is used. An interactive joint control on the unchanged Models.NecessarilyUnderived.rotating interpretation establishes both distinct necessary individuals have the potential role, every world has well-founded present support, but the cross-world union is not well-founded: replacing union WF with worldwise WF fails. No identification of ordinary causation with metaphysical grounding is asserted; selecting causal edges for the support relation is an explicit restricted profile. Reject the proposed weakening to merely an inhabited root-accessible family without further conditions: a root→middle→outside frame can have both individuals present only at middle; potential witnesses at outside then need not have existing sources. Necessity at the root does not imply presence at that two-step successor without transitivity, and Ontic does not assume endpoint soundness. This precise rejected weakening is a proof-boundary analysis, not yet a kernel-certified three-world control. A no-successor frame also makes necessary/potential roles vacuous, so actual reflexivity cannot simply be dropped.
